A read-only rating is one image named by `getValueLabel`, and it shows any score, like an average.

Stars only grow on hover and shrink on press when motion is allowed. On touch screens each star gets extra padding, and in forced colors mode filled stars use the text color and empty ones use the system’s gray.
Stars run from the right, and a half star fills from its right edge.

UI SDK adds a little CSS of its own in a cascade layer named `ui-sdk`. Declare that layer at the top of your global stylesheet, above the Tailwind import, so your classes win over it.
With `deselectable`, pressing the checked star again clears the score.
With `step={0.5}`, each half of a star is its own radio, and the arrow keys move by half a star.
With a `name`, the score submits with the form. `required` blocks submission until there’s a score, with the browser’s own message.

`Rating` renders its child once per star, so put one `RatingItem` inside it. Each star draws an empty star with a filled one clipped to `--rating-fill`, so half stars and averages like 4.3 show exactly.
`size` is `sm`, `default` or `lg`.
